I am a bit confused; in this comment, you come off as quite antagonist and dismissive of the issue being raised because it doesn't affect the way you play Corpo
but then in this comment,

and this comment as well, you acknowledge both that BIAV is implementing new mechanics which could directly negatively impact your Pollux runs, in addition to acknowledging that this is demonstrably a course of action that could directly lead to further unannounced "fixes" which result in lowered character performances.

My curiosity comes from the dichotomy between these two viewpoints; may I ask why you believe this is "whining" and meaningless and should be dismissed, while also acknowledging that "shadow fixes" can result in performance hits affecting existing player investments?

I am unsure if this comes from a more self-centric viewpoint where the understanding is that issues are not relevant until they directly affect you in some way, or if it comes from a more short-sighted outlook on overall game balance where the understanding is that existing patterns of behavior do not correlate to possible future actions. 

I'm not trying to be antagonistic, I'm merely just curious as I see this level of response quite often coming from people unaffected by changes when speaking to people who are. When issues like this occur, I see them both as something that directly negatively impacts existing investments, in addition to demonstrating problematic behavior patterns which are likely to repeat in the future. I don't think I possess the capability to decouple the impact on others with the future possibility of impacting me, so I'm just curious as to exactly drives this kind of response since you seem to be aware of both.

Additionally, to other users who may have a mindset of "this is an irrelevant issue which does not affect my investments or how I play the character", please keep in mind that similar issues have occurred in the past, establishing a pattern of behavior which will likely result in similar things occurring in the future as well. For those seeking evidence, you may check an unannounced shadow nerf to Lily under the stated reasoning of a "bugfix", which reduced her poison application capabilities by almost 50% as of that patch in addition to introducing a *new* bug at the exact same time which reduced it further to *beyond* 50% (some may consider this a rather distinctive example of situational irony <:GDoll_serenity:1468257540809822302>)

As evidence, you can reference my reproduction of the same setup pre-patch vs post-patch under the same buffs and situation (https://discord.com/channels/1131791637933199470/1512453677846237335/1512459417877221526), where Lily's poison application was directly nerfed from +3133 per tick (pre-patch) to +1410 per tick (post-patch), which was a 55% nerf. This was, in part, due to a new bug introduced in the same patch where Lily no longer benefited from Xu's Spellbound poison amplification effect, but that particular bug has since been fixed. As further evidence, you may reference a new clip attached to this message, taken today, reproducing again the exact same team and situation, where you can see that Lily's current poison tick is now +1782 per tick, which is a -43% performance nerf as a direct result of an unannounced "bugfix" that has existed since her initial release over one and a half years ago.

While this event mostly flew under the radar of most users and resulted in little to no backlash because poison application Lily was a very niche build used by a minority of the playerbase, the fact that it occurred at all is something I would consider a relevant data point when establishing a behavioral pattern for things which could occur in the future. Even if this doesn't affect anything you play now, what is the guarantee that it won't eventually affect something you do play? For now, you do not speak for others because you are not affected. But at that point, who will speak for you?

I think there's a case to be made here that there's a distinct difference between a "change" - i.e., something that is bad for one person but could be beneficial for someone else, and a "nerf" - i.e., something that is strictly either bad or neutral for everyone

In this case, I'd classify the pilot change as the latter, because there is no situation where this has resulted in a positive result for *anyone*. Either it has been bad for someone, or it has not changed. That means that there is no situation where it is good for someone

If something is bad for you but good for someone else, then there's much more nuance at hand because it benefits someone so changing or reverting it would then remove that benefit which is then bad for them, so there's no easy solution

If something is bad for you but good for nobody, then that just strictly becomes a net negative across the board period, even if you are unaffected. I think that is the core issue at point here, is that many of these changes are direct nerfs which, even if you are an unaffected party who is neutral on the change, provide no benefit in any way while negatively impacting many others at the same time. Personally I believe it's hard to justify or stand behind such directly negative changes no matter whether you are affected or not

content:
as a new player (2 weeks) that was around before the shop updated, this actually really annoys me. the addition of the gnosis at the same rate was an actual nice qol change, but this price hike is ridiculous (especially so for the advanced skill materials).

there's a benefit to having 1 whole item in the shop vs buying the shards (it makes the items more tangible since it's vastly easier to keep track of how many rose scrips you have than to keep track of how many aetheric shards & mimetic crystals you have in addition to the rose scrip cost of them), but this is honestly the wrong direction.

you do get more aetheric stones faster (3 in 1 month with the new shop vs 1 in 2 months with the old shop) so the price increase can at least be justified a little (except it punishes players that didn't mind waiting), but with advanced skill materials it's a 51.5% increase in price for all units just to have 1 more every single month (3 in 1 month with new shop vs 2 in 1 month with old shop).

this honestly just seems like a way to force people to buy the battle pass. this along with reading other posts in the forum about recent and past changes doesn't paint a good impression for me to becoming a long time player.

**the solution to the problem is simple in my opinion: just offer both options** (the cheaper aetheric shards and mimetic crystals along with the more expensive advanced skill materials and aetheric stones). that way you're still paying a premium for getting more faster, but the option to slowly accumulate them at a cheaper price exists and those players aren't punished.
